processed.title: Glis1 regulates metabolic programming by promoting H3K18 lactylation to alleviate neuronal senescence following spinal cord injury.

figures.label: Figure 1
figures.caption: Neuronal senescence exists following SCI, with elevated levels of lactate and H3K18 lactylation. (A,B) After lipopolysaccharide (LPS) treatment, SASP expression levels and quantification results were detected by Western blot. (C,D) Immunofluorescence was used to detect the expression level and quantitative analysis of neuronal senescence markers. (E) Neuronal viability determined by CCK-8 assay in each group. (F,G) The expression level and quantitative analysis of SASP in the sham group and SCI group were detected by Western blotting (WB). (H,I) Representative images and quantification results of immunofluorescence detection of the expression levels of aging markers in spinal cord tissue. (J) Intracellular lactate content was measured using a lactate detection kit. (K) Global histone lactylation modification levels in neuronal cells measured by WB. (L,M) Representative images and quantification results of panlactylation and H3K18la levels of neuronal histones detected by immunofluorescence. (N,O) WB detection and quantitative analysis of histone lactylation modification sites in neuronal cells. (P) Co-immunoprecipitation of H3K18la. (Q,R) WB was used to detect and quantify the overall lactylation level and H3K18 lactylation level in the Sham group and the SCI group. (S,T) Representative images and quantitative results of histone lactylation before and after SCI detected by immunofluorescence. ( n = 3. The relative contents were calculated using ImageJ software. All the data are expressed as the mean ± SD, and one- or two-way ANOVA followed by Tukey's post hoc test was applied. ∗ p < 0.05, ∗∗ p < 0.01, ∗∗∗ p < 0.001, ∗∗∗∗ p < 0.0001 vs. Control/Sham.

figures.label: Figure 2
figures.caption: Glis1 inhibits neuronal senescence by promoting H3K18 lactylation. (A) After lipopolysaccharide (LPS) treatment, Glis1 expression levels and quantification results were detected by Western blot. (B) Immunofluorescence detection and quantification of Glis1 expression levels before and after LPS treatment. (C) Neuronal viability determined by CCK-8 assay in each group after treatment. (D,E) The expression levels and quantitative analysis of senescence markers of Glis1 after different treatments were detected by WB. (F) Representative images of the expression levels of senescence markers detected by immunofluorescence. (G) Representative images of neuron panlactylation and H3K18 lactylation levels detected by immunofluorescence. (H) Quantitative analysis results of representative immunofluorescence images. (I,J) Panlactylation and H3K18la levels were detected and quantified by WB. (K,L) Expression and quantitative analysis of glycolysis-related genes in neuronal cells after different treatments by WB. (M) Determination of the NAD + /NADH ratio in neuronal cells. (N–Q) Extracellular acidification rate (ECAR) and cellular oxygen consumption (OCR) of neuronal cells. ( n = 3. The relative contents were calculated using ImageJ software. All the data are expressed as the mean ± SD, and one- or two-way ANOVA followed by Tukey's post hoc test was applied. ∗ p < 0.05, ∗∗ p < 0.01, ∗∗∗ p < 0.001, ∗∗∗∗ p < 0.0001 vs. Control; # p < 0.05, ## p < 0.01, ### p < 0.001, #### p < 0.0001 vs. LPS; & p < 0.05, && p < 0.01, &&& p < 0.001, &&&& p < 0.0001 vs. LPS + si-Glis1.

figures.label: Figure 3
figures.caption: SCG2 was identified as a potential downstream target of H3K18la, and H3K18la activated SCG2 transcription in neuronal cells. (A) Distribution of H3K18la sites relative to the translation start site (TSS). (B,C) Distribution of peaks enriched by H3K18la on the genome of neuronal cells. (D) Analysis of the H3K18la peaks by the Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG). (E) Heatmap of differentially expressed genes in the control group, the lipopolysaccharide (LPS) group, and the LPS + Glis1 group. (F,G) GO and KEGG enrichment analysis of the regulatory pathways in the LPS group and the LPS + pc-Glis1 group. (H) The process of screening SCG2 as a potential downstream target regulated by H3K18la through bioinformatics analysis. (I) Schematic diagram of the division of the SCG2 promoter region. (J,K) ChIP analysis results between H3K18la and each region of the SCG2 promoter. (L) A series of plasmids containing the 5′ unidirectional deletion of the SCG2 gene promoter region fused with the luciferase gene were transfected into neuronal cells. (M) Schematic diagram of the inhibition of histone lactylation by glycolysis inhibitors. (N) Double luciferase assays for H3K18la and SCG2 with or without OXAMATE and pc-Glis1 treatment. (O,P) ChIP analysis of H3K18la and SCG2 with or without OXAMATE treatment. (Q) Detection of intracellular lactate content with or without OXAMATE treatment using a lactate detection kit. (R) Western blotting detection of the expression levels and quantification of H3K18la and SCG2 with or without OXAMATE treatment ( n = 3). All the data are expressed as the mean ± SD, and one- or two-way ANOVA followed by Tukey's post hoc test was applied. ∗ p < 0.05, ∗∗ p < 0.01, ∗∗∗ p < 0.001, ∗∗∗∗ p < 0.0001 vs. Control; # p < 0.05, ## p < 0.01, ### p < 0.001, #### p < 0.0001 vs. LPS; & p < 0.05, && p < 0.01, &&& p < 0.001, &&&& p < 0.0001 vs. pc-Glis1; ˆ p < 0.05, ^ p < 0.01, ^^ p < 0.001, ^^^ p < 0.0001 vs. Region1.

figures.label: Figure 4
figures.caption: SCG2 is capable of undergoing metabolic reprogramming and forming a negative feedback loop with H3K18la, thereby regulating neuronal senescence. (A–D) Extracellular acidification rate (ECAR) and oxygen consumption rate (OCR) experiments of neuronal cells treated with or without lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and pc-SCG2. (E) Detection of intracellular lactate content in cells treated with or without LPS and pc-SCG2 using a lactate detection kit. (F) Chromatin immunoprecipitation analysis of the binding of the SCG2 promoter to H3K18la after overexpression of SCG2 and lactate treatment. (G–I) Western blotting detection and quantitative analysis of the contents of Glis1, H3K18la, aging markers, and glycolysis-related proteins. (J,K) Representative images and quantitative results of SA-β-gal levels analyzed by immunofluorescence ( n = 3). The relative contents were calculated using ImageJ software. All the data are expressed as the mean ± SD, and one- or two-way ANOVA followed by Tukey's post hoc test was applied. ∗ p < 0.05, ∗∗ p < 0.01, ∗∗∗ p < 0.001, ∗∗∗∗ p < 0.0001 vs. Control; # p < 0.05, ## p < 0.01, ### p < 0.001, #### p < 0.0001 vs. LPS; % p < 0.05, %% p < 0.01, %%% p < 0.001, %%%% p < 0.0001 vs. LPS + pc-SCG2.

figures.label: Figure 5
figures.caption: Glis1 can modulate p300, thereby promoting H3K18la lactylation. (A) The potential binding modes and affinities between the unmodified H3K18 peptide and candidate enzymes (p300, MOF, GCN5, and TIP60) were predicted using AutoDock Vina. (B,C) The expression levels of p300, MOF, GCN5, and TIP60 after lipopolysaccharide (LPS) treatment were detected by Western blotting and quantitatively analyzed. (D) The binding of H3K18la and p300 was verified by co-immunoprecipitation. (E) Representative images and quantitative analysis of the colocalization of H3K18la and p300 by immunofluorescence were performed. (F,G) Representative images and quantitative results of the levels of Glis1, p300, H3K18la, and SCG2 after overexpression of Glis1 and p300 were analyzed by immunofluorescence. (H) The intracellular lactate content in cells treated with LPS and overexpressing Glis1 and p300 was detected using a lactate detection kit. (I) The expression levels of H3K18la, H3K18ac, and H3K27ac after LPS and overexpression of Glis1 and p300 were detected by Western blotting and quantitatively analyzed. (J) The binding of H3K18la, H3K18ac, and H3K27ac with p300 after LPS and overexpression of Glis1 was verified by co-immunoprecipitation ( n = 3). All the data are expressed as the mean ± SD, and one- or two-way ANOVA followed by Tukey's post hoc test was applied. ∗ p < 0.05, ∗∗ p < 0.01, ∗∗∗ p < 0.001, ∗∗∗∗ p < 0.0001 vs. Control; # p < 0.05, ## p < 0.01, ### p < 0.001, #### p < 0.0001 vs. LPS; ˆ p < 0.05, ^ p < 0.01, ^^ p < 0.001, ˆ^^^ p < 0.0001 vs. LPS + pc-Glis1.

figures.label: Figure 6
figures.caption: Glis1 regulates the expression of SCG2 by promoting the expression of p300/H3K18la, thereby inhibiting aging and promoting angiogenesis. (A) Western blotting was employed to detect the expression levels and quantitative results of p300, H3K18la, SCG2, and aging-related markers after lipopolysaccharide (LPS) treatment, overexpression of Glis1, and treatment with or without OXAMATE. (B,C) Immunofluorescence was utilized to detect representative images and quantitative analysis of the expression of p300, H3K18la, SCG2, and aging-related markers after LPS treatment, overexpression of Glis1, and with or without OXAMATE treatment. (D,E) Migration assays of HUVECs cultured in CM derived from primary neurons with the indicated treatments (control, LPS, LPS + pc-Glis1, and LPS + pc-Glis1+OXAMATE). (F,G) Tube formation assays of HUVECs cultured in neuronal CM from the respective treatment groups (scale bar: 200 μm). (H) Neuronal viability determined by CCK-8 assay in each group after LPS treatment, overexpression of Glis1, and OXAMATE treatment ( n = 3). The relative contents were calculated using ImageJ software. All the data are expressed as the mean ± SD, and one- or two-way ANOVA followed by Tukey's post hoc test was applied. ∗ p < 0.05, ∗∗ p < 0.01, ∗∗∗ p < 0.001, ∗∗∗∗ p < 0.0001 vs. Control; # p < 0.05, ## p < 0.01, ### p < 0.001, #### p < 0.0001 vs. LPS; & p < 0.05, && p < 0.01, &&& p < 0.001, &&&& p < 0.0001 vs. LPS + pc-Glis1.

figures.label: Figure 7
figures.caption: Glis1 promotes the expression of p300/H3K18la in rats, thereby regulating the expression of SCG2, inhibiting aging, and alleviating SCI. (A) Representative T2-weighted magnetic resonance (MR) images of the spinal cords in each group ( n = 3). (B,C) Western blot detection of p300, H3K18la, SCG2, aging markers, and neuron regeneration markers in each group. (D) Quantitative analysis of p300, H3K18la, SCG2, aging markers, and neuron regeneration markers in spinal cord tissues after different treatments by WB. (E) Representative images of the expression level of SA-β-gal in spinal cord tissues detected by immunofluorescence. (F) Representative images of the expression level of NF in spinal cord tissues detected by immunofluorescence. (G) Representative images of the expression level of GFAP in spinal cord tissues detected by immunofluorescence. (H) Representative images of the expression level of Tuj-1 in spinal cord tissues detected by immunofluorescence. (I) Representative images of the expression level of CD31 in spinal cord tissues detected by immunofluorescence. (J) Quantitative analysis of immunofluorescence in each group. (The relative contents were calculated using ImageJ software. All the data are expressed as the mean ± SD, and one- or two-way ANOVA followed by Tukey's post hoc test was applied. # p < 0.05, ## p < 0.01, ### p < 0.001, #### p < 0.0001 vs. Sham.

figures.label: Figure 8
figures.caption: Specimen and pathological staining of the rat spinal cord. (A–C) Representative hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) (A), Nissl (B), and Masson staining (C) of spinal cord tissues in each group ( n = 3). (D) The gross appearances of spinal cord tissues in each group. (E) BBB scores of different groups at 3, 7, 14, 21, and 28 days after SCI or sham surgery ( n = 3). (The relative contents were calculated using ImageJ software. All the data are expressed as the mean ± SD, and one- or two-way ANOVA followed by Tukey's post hoc test was applied. # p < 0.05, ## p < 0.01, ### p < 0.001, #### p < 0.0001 vs. Sham.

figures.label: Figure 9
figures.caption: Glis1 initiates H3K18 lactylation via p300 and regulates the expression of downstream SCG2. The negative feedback loop among the expression of SCG2, glycolytic metabolism, and H3K18la modification undergoes metabolic reprogramming, thereby suppressing neuronal senescence.
